review_findings.output_leakage: none. solve() gets demos plus the query grid. The gate and evidence wrapper read only query['input'] (proved with LabelFree). Labels are used only by verify() after the program runs.
review_findings.hidden_parameter_inference: none. d4 is unused, and palette only sets ZERO=palette[0] and TCOL=palette[2]. The template is read from visible TCOL cells.
review_findings.fallbacks: none. There is no first, majority or intersection pick, no demo skipping and no reset. The program raises Abstain when there are no survivors, when a survivor is undefined on the query, or when survivors disagree.
review_findings.d4_choice: none. The 8 raster scans are included as a full D4-closed set, and unanimity is required.
review_findings.domain_narrowing: none. The query is never resampled (250 queries drawn, 0 dropped). Only demos are resampled, from the unmodified native generator, and only when the gate finds survivor disagreement. Native size and sprite domain are unrestricted.
review_findings.correctness_argument: Every native random-branch label equals 'paint every open fit': draw() rejects unplanned fits and overlaps, and duplicate sprite cells trip the red check. That truth hypothesis is in the family and survives every native demo set, so any unanimous answer on native data equals the native label.
review_findings.ambiguity_class: Context shortfall, not intrinsic. Rivals differ only through the thick/line filters, and native demos with thin or bar templates refute them with positive probability. The data agree: 0 queries unresolved after the cap, and at most 3 resamples were needed.
review_findings.constructor_note: validate() ignores draw()'s legality result. Canonical train pairs 0 (bar) and 1 (diamond) are latent-labelled, illegal draws. A witness with identical input and a different output is shown in e5062a87_tests.py. The fixture is kept unchanged: its own demos refute all-fits, and all 30 fixture survivors agree on the canonical test. No constructor change is required for certification. The optional host fix would be to assert draw()'s return value in validate().
non_blocking_remarks: The 120-hypothesis family (holes/centre/thick/line/resolution) was chosen so that it could explain the latent-labelled canonical demos. It is a finite stated scope, not a proof of universal identifiability.

About 14% of fresh native episodes need demo resampling. Without the evidence gate in dispatch, those episodes would fail verify(), because the program abstains, and would be dropped. Wiring the gate makes the rejection explicit and label-free.
